::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 16th 1894  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Bodleian Library, Oxford: MS English Letters: e.174 ff 1
:::

Dear [Mr Bullock](people/person_221.qmd),
I do not know Canterbury well enough to attempt it. I have only seen it three times cursorily once on the day of the [Archbishop](people/person_140.qmd)’s installation- the best person to undertake it would be

[Miss Jenner](people/person_762.qmd)[^1]
Preston Vicarage
Wingham
Dover

[Bishop Jenner](people/person_758.qmd)’s daughter who knows the Cathedral well and has a good deal of power of writing

I think I could do Salisbury

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Bishop Jenner had four daughters of whom Amabel Jenner (b.1876/7), who published plays and fiction, seems the most likely to be referred to here.  Bullock had evidently asked CMY to contribute an account of Canterbury Cathedral to his *Daily Lections* project.
